meta.title: From the Divided Kingdom to Ezra and Nehemiah
meta.chronology: Kings' dates follow Edwin R. Thiele, The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings (3rd ed., 1983), as tabulated in the Wikipedia article 'Kings of Israel and Judah' (sole reigns). Where the Bible's reign length includes a co-regency, the co-regency is shown as a lighter extension of the bar.
meta.chronologyShort: Edwin R. Thiele, The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings.

certainty.fixed: Fixed: confirmed by a dated record outside the Bible (Assyrian, Babylonian or Egyptian).
certainty.calculated: Calculated: worked out from the Bible's own dating (reign lengths, or 'in the Nth year of King X'), anchored to fixed dates. Kings of Israel and Judah follow Thiele's chronology.
certainty.approx: Approximate: the Bible places it within a reign or period but gives no exact year.
certainty.disputed: Disputed: Bible-believing scholars hold different views on the date.

rulers.name: Shishak (Shoshenq I)
rulers.summary: Founder of Egypt's 22nd dynasty. Invaded Judah and Israel in Rehoboam's fifth year and carried off the temple treasures.

rulers.name: Shalmaneser III
rulers.summary: Not named in the Bible, but his inscriptions name two kings of Israel: Ahab at the Battle of Qarqar (853 BC) and Jehu paying tribute (841 BC). These two dates anchor the whole chronology of the kings.

rulers.name: Hazael of Damascus
rulers.summary: Elijah was told to anoint him (1 Kings 19:15); Elisha wept over the harm he would do to Israel. He took much of Israel's territory east of the Jordan.

rulers.name: Tiglath-pileser III (Pul)
rulers.summary: Revived Assyria's power. Took tribute from Menahem and Ahaz, captured Damascus and deported the people of Galilee and Gilead.

rulers.name: Rezin of Damascus
rulers.summary: Last king of Aram-Damascus. Allied with Pekah of Israel against Ahaz; killed when Assyria took Damascus.

rulers.name: Shalmaneser V
rulers.summary: Besieged Samaria after Hoshea stopped paying tribute.

rulers.name: Sargon II
rulers.summary: Claimed the capture of Samaria in his inscriptions. Named in the Bible only in Isaiah 20:1; his existence was doubted by critics until his palace was excavated in the 1840s.

rulers.name: Merodach-baladan
rulers.summary: Babylonian king who sent envoys to Hezekiah. Isaiah warned that Babylon would one day carry off everything Hezekiah showed them.

rulers.name: Sennacherib
rulers.summary: Invaded Judah in 701 BC and took Lachish, but Jerusalem was delivered. Killed by his sons in Nineveh, as Isaiah foretold.

rulers.name: Tirhakah (Taharqa)
rulers.summary: Cushite ruler of Egypt who marched out against Sennacherib. His dates as pharaoh are 690-664 BC; in 701 BC he led the army as a prince.

rulers.name: Esarhaddon
rulers.summary: Son and successor of Sennacherib. His inscriptions list Manasseh of Judah among his vassal kings.

rulers.name: Nabopolassar
rulers.summary: Founder of the Neo-Babylonian Empire; destroyed Nineveh with the Medes in 612 BC. Father of Nebuchadnezzar.

rulers.name: Pharaoh Neco II
rulers.summary: Killed Josiah at Megiddo, deposed Jehoahaz and installed Jehoiakim. Defeated by Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish.

rulers.name: Nebuchadnezzar II
rulers.summary: Greatest king of Babylon. Took Daniel and Jehoiachin captive and destroyed Jerusalem and the temple in 586 BC. Jeremiah calls him the LORD's servant in judging the nations (Jeremiah 27:6).

rulers.name: Pharaoh Hophra (Apries)
rulers.summary: His army briefly drew the Babylonians away from Jerusalem. Jeremiah foretold he would be handed over to his enemies.

rulers.name: Evil-merodach (Amel-Marduk)
rulers.summary: Released Jehoiachin from prison in Babylon.

rulers.name: Nabonidus & Belshazzar
rulers.summary: Nabonidus was the last king of Babylon; his son Belshazzar ruled in Babylon on his behalf. Critics once said Belshazzar never existed. Babylonian texts later confirmed him, which also explains why he could only offer Daniel the third place in the kingdom (Daniel 5:16).

rulers.name: Cyrus the Great
rulers.summary: Named by Isaiah long before his birth as the LORD's shepherd who would rebuild Jerusalem. Conquered Babylon and allowed the exiles to return.

rulers.name: Cambyses II
rulers.summary: Son of Cyrus; added Egypt to the Persian Empire in 525 BC. Not named in the Bible.

rulers.name: Darius I (the Great)
rulers.summary: Confirmed Cyrus's decree after it was found in the archives at Ecbatana, and paid for the temple to be finished. Haggai and Zechariah date their prophecies by his reign.

rulers.name: Xerxes I (Ahasuerus)
rulers.summary: The king of the book of Esther, reigning from Susa over 127 provinces from India to Cush.

rulers.name: Artaxerxes I
rulers.summary: Sent Ezra to teach the Law in Jerusalem (his 7th year) and Nehemiah to rebuild its walls (his 20th year).

kings.name: Jeroboam I
kings.summary: Solomon's official who led the ten northern tribes away from the house of David. Set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan: "the sin of Jeroboam" that later northern kings are measured by.

kings.name: Nadab
kings.summary: Son of Jeroboam. Killed by Baasha while besieging Gibbethon, ending Jeroboam's dynasty as the prophet Ahijah had foretold.

kings.name: Baasha
kings.summary: Seized the throne and destroyed Jeroboam's family. Reigned from Tirzah and fought Asa of Judah.

kings.name: Elah
kings.summary: Son of Baasha. Murdered while drunk in Tirzah by Zimri, one of his chariot commanders.

kings.name: Zimri
kings.summary: Reigned seven days. When the army made Omri king, Zimri burned the palace in Tirzah down on himself.

kings.name: Tibni
kings.summary: Rival king followed by half the people after Zimri's death. Omri's side prevailed.

kings.name: Omri
kings.summary: Army commander who founded a powerful dynasty and built Samaria as Israel's new capital.
kings.evidence: The Moabite Mesha Stele names "Omri king of Israel", and Assyrian records call Israel "the house of Omri" long after his death.

kings.name: Ahab
kings.summary: Married Jezebel of Sidon and promoted Baal worship, opposed by Elijah. Killed in battle at Ramoth-gilead.
kings.evidence: Shalmaneser III's Kurkh Monolith lists "Ahab the Israelite" with 2,000 chariots at the Battle of Qarqar, 853 BC.

kings.name: Ahaziah
kings.summary: Son of Ahab. Injured in a fall, he sent to ask Baal-zebub instead of the LORD, and died as Elijah foretold.

kings.name: Joram (Jehoram)
kings.summary: Son of Ahab. Fought Moab alongside Jehoshaphat; Samaria survived an Aramean siege in his reign. Killed by Jehu at Jezreel.

kings.name: Jehu
kings.summary: Anointed at Elisha's command to judge the house of Ahab. Wiped out Baal worship in Israel, but kept Jeroboam's golden calves.
kings.evidence: The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III shows Jehu bowing with tribute in 841 BC. It is the only known picture of an Israelite king.

kings.name: Jehoahaz
kings.summary: Israel was crushed by Hazael of Aram. Jehoahaz sought the LORD, who gave Israel a deliverer.

kings.name: Jehoash (Joash)
kings.summary: Visited the dying Elisha and won back towns from Aram, as Elisha foretold. Defeated Amaziah of Judah and broke down Jerusalem's wall.

kings.name: Jeroboam II
kings.summary: Restored Israel's borders as Jonah had prophesied. A time of wealth and injustice condemned by Amos and Hosea.
kings.note: 2 Kings 14:23 gives him 41 years. Thiele counts them from 793 BC, when he began ruling alongside his father.

kings.name: Zechariah
kings.summary: Last of Jehu's dynasty, fulfilling the promise of four generations (2 Kings 10:30). Assassinated after six months.

kings.name: Shallum
kings.summary: Assassinated Zechariah and reigned one month before being killed by Menahem.

kings.name: Menahem
kings.summary: Seized Samaria by force. Paid a thousand talents of silver to Pul (Tiglath-pileser III) of Assyria.
kings.evidence: Tiglath-pileser III's annals list "Menahem of Samaria" among the kings who paid him tribute.

kings.name: Pekahiah
kings.summary: Son of Menahem. Assassinated in his palace by his officer Pekah.

kings.name: Pekah
kings.summary: Allied with Rezin of Damascus against Judah. Lost Galilee and Gilead to Assyria and was killed by Hoshea.
kings.note: 2 Kings 15:27 gives him 20 years. Thiele counts them from 752 BC as a rival reign east of the Jordan, overlapping Menahem and Pekahiah.

kings.name: Hoshea
kings.summary: Last king of Israel. Rebelled against Assyria; Samaria fell after a three-year siege and the people were deported.
kings.evidence: Tiglath-pileser III's annals claim he put Hoshea on the throne after Pekah was overthrown.

kings.name: Rehoboam
kings.summary: Solomon's son. His harsh answer at Shechem split the kingdom. Shishak of Egypt plundered Jerusalem in his fifth year.

kings.name: Abijah (Abijam)
kings.summary: Fought Jeroboam. Chronicles records his speech appealing to the LORD's covenant with David.

kings.name: Asa
kings.summary: Removed idols and reformed worship. Later relied on the king of Aram instead of the LORD against Baasha.

kings.name: Jehoshaphat
kings.summary: Strengthened Judah and sent officials to teach the Law. Unwisely allied himself with Ahab's family.
kings.note: Thiele places a co-regency with his father Asa from 873 BC (Asa was diseased in his feet, 1 Kings 15:23).

kings.name: Jehoram
kings.summary: Married Ahab's daughter Athaliah and followed the ways of Ahab. Edom revolted in his reign.
kings.note: Thiele places a co-regency with Jehoshaphat from 853 BC.

kings.name: Ahaziah
kings.summary: Son of Athaliah. Killed by Jehu while visiting Joram of Israel; died at Megiddo.

kings.name: Athaliah (queen)
kings.summary: Ahab's daughter. Seized the throne and tried to wipe out David's royal line; overthrown by Jehoiada the priest.

kings.name: Joash (Jehoash)
kings.summary: Hidden as a baby in the temple and crowned at seven. Repaired the temple under Jehoiada, but after Jehoiada died he turned away and had Jehoiada's son Zechariah stoned.

kings.name: Amaziah
kings.summary: Defeated Edom but then worshipped Edom's gods. Defeated by Jehoash of Israel and later murdered at Lachish.

kings.name: Uzziah (Azariah)
kings.summary: Long and prosperous reign. Struck with leprosy for burning incense in the temple, so his son Jotham governed for him.
kings.note: 2 Kings 15:2 gives him 52 years. Thiele counts them from 792 BC, when he began ruling alongside his father Amaziah.

kings.name: Jotham
kings.summary: Built the upper gate of the temple and grew powerful because he walked steadily before the LORD.
kings.note: Governed for his father Uzziah from about 750 BC (2 Kings 15:5).

kings.name: Ahaz
kings.summary: Refused Isaiah's call to trust the LORD and paid Assyria for help instead. Copied a pagan altar from Damascus and sacrificed his own son.
kings.evidence: Tiglath-pileser III's annals list "Jehoahaz [Ahaz] of Judah" among the kings paying tribute.

kings.name: Hezekiah
kings.summary: Trusted the LORD like no other king of Judah. Restored temple worship, was delivered from Sennacherib, and was granted fifteen more years of life.
kings.evidence: Hezekiah's water tunnel (2 Kings 20:20) still runs under Jerusalem, and a clay seal impression bearing his name was found there in 2015.

kings.name: Manasseh
kings.summary: Reigned longest of all and rebuilt pagan shrines, shedding much innocent blood. Chronicles records his captivity, repentance and restoration (2 Chronicles 33:11-13).
kings.note: Thiele places a co-regency with Hezekiah from 696 BC.
kings.evidence: Inscriptions of Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal list "Manasseh king of Judah" among their vassals.

kings.name: Amon
kings.summary: Followed his father's idolatry. Murdered by his servants after two years.

kings.name: Josiah
kings.summary: Became king at eight. When the Book of the Law was found he led Judah's deepest reform, of whom it is said no king turned to the LORD as he did (2 Kings 23:25). Killed at Megiddo opposing Pharaoh Neco.

kings.name: Jehoahaz
kings.summary: Reigned three months before Pharaoh Neco imprisoned him at Riblah and took him to Egypt.

kings.name: Jehoiakim
kings.summary: Put on the throne by Neco. Burned Jeremiah's scroll and rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.

kings.name: Jehoiachin
kings.summary: Surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar after three months and was taken to Babylon. Released from prison 37 years later.
kings.evidence: Ration tablets from Babylon list oil given to "Jehoiachin, king of Judah" and his sons.

kings.name: Zedekiah
kings.summary: Last king of Judah. Ignored Jeremiah's warnings and rebelled. Jerusalem fell; he was blinded at Riblah and taken to Babylon.

prophets.name: Elijah
prophets.summary: Prophet to the northern kingdom in the days of Ahab and Ahaziah. Confronted Baal worship on Mount Carmel and was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind.
prophets.basis: Active in the reigns of Ahab and Ahaziah of Israel.

prophets.name: Elisha
prophets.summary: Elijah's successor, who received a double portion of his spirit. His ministry was marked by many miracles of provision, healing and deliverance.
prophets.basis: Called in Ahab's reign; died in the reign of Jehoash of Israel (2 Kings 13:14).

prophets.name: Jonah
prophets.summary: From Gath-hepher in Galilee. Fled toward Tarshish rather than preach to Nineveh, but the city repented at his message. Jesus pointed to Jonah as a sign of his own death and resurrection.
prophets.basis: Prophesied in the reign of Jeroboam II (2 Kings 14:25).

prophets.name: Amos
prophets.summary: A shepherd from Tekoa in Judah sent to the northern kingdom. Denounced injustice and empty religion at Bethel.
prophets.basis: Amos 1:1: in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam II, two years before the earthquake.

prophets.name: Hosea
prophets.summary: Prophet to Israel whose marriage to an unfaithful wife pictured the LORD's faithful love for unfaithful Israel.
prophets.basis: Hosea 1:1: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah of Judah, and Jeroboam II of Israel.

prophets.name: Isaiah
prophets.summary: Prophet in Jerusalem through four reigns. Called in a vision of the LORD's holiness; foretold the virgin-born Immanuel and the suffering Servant.
prophets.basis: Called in the year Uzziah died (Isaiah 6:1); records Sennacherib's death in 681 BC (Isaiah 37:38).

prophets.name: Micah
prophets.summary: From Moresheth in Judah's lowlands. Spoke against Samaria and Jerusalem, and foretold that the ruler of Israel would come from Bethlehem.
prophets.basis: Micah 1:1: in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah.

prophets.name: Nahum
prophets.summary: Announced the fall of Nineveh, capital of Assyria.
prophets.basis: Written after the fall of Thebes (663 BC, Nahum 3:8) and before Nineveh fell (612 BC).

prophets.name: Zephaniah
prophets.summary: Warned of the day of the LORD, and promised the LORD would rejoice over a restored remnant.
prophets.basis: Zephaniah 1:1: in the days of Josiah.

prophets.name: Jeremiah
prophets.summary: Priest's son from Anathoth who warned Judah for forty years before and after Jerusalem's fall. Promised a new covenant written on the heart.
prophets.basis: Called in Josiah's 13th year (Jeremiah 1:2), 627 BC; last seen taken to Egypt after 586 BC.

prophets.name: Habakkuk
prophets.summary: Wrestled with God over the rise of Babylon, and learned that the righteous shall live by faith.
prophets.basis: Speaks of the Chaldeans (Babylonians) as a rising power (Habakkuk 1:6).

prophets.name: Daniel
prophets.summary: Taken to Babylon as a young man. Served kings of Babylon and Persia while staying faithful to God; received visions of the kingdoms to come.
prophets.basis: Taken in 605 BC (Daniel 1:1); last dated vision in the third year of Cyrus (Daniel 10:1).

prophets.name: Ezekiel
prophets.summary: Priest among the exiles by the Chebar canal. Saw the glory of the LORD leave the temple, and the vision of dry bones brought back to life.
prophets.basis: Called in the 5th year of Jehoiachin's exile (Ezekiel 1:2); last dated oracle in the 27th year (Ezekiel 29:17).

prophets.name: Haggai
prophets.summary: Rebuked the returned exiles for living in panelled houses while the LORD's house lay in ruins, and promised that the latter glory of this house would be greater than the former.
prophets.basis: All four messages are dated to the 2nd year of Darius (Haggai 1:1; 2:10).

prophets.name: Zechariah
prophets.summary: Encouraged the temple builders: "Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD." Foretold the King coming to Jerusalem humble and riding on a donkey.
prophets.basis: Dated messages from the 2nd to the 4th year of Darius (Zechariah 1:1; 7:1).

prophets.name: Malachi
prophets.summary: The last of the Old Testament prophets. Confronted careless worship and broken marriages, and promised the messenger who would prepare the way of the LORD.
prophets.basis: The book is undated, but the sins it addresses (corrupt priests, marriage to foreign wives, neglect of tithes) match Nehemiah 13, so it is usually placed in Nehemiah's time.

events.title: The kingdom divides
events.summary: At Shechem the northern tribes reject Solomon's son Rehoboam and make Jeroboam king. The prophet Ahijah had foretold this as the LORD's judgment on Solomon's idolatry. Judah and Benjamin stay with the house of David.

events.title: Golden calves at Bethel and Dan
events.summary: To stop his people going up to the temple in Jerusalem, Jeroboam sets up two golden calves and his own priesthood. A man of God foretells that a king named Josiah will one day burn the bones of these priests on the Bethel altar.

events.title: Shishak invades Judah
events.summary: In Rehoboam's fifth year Pharaoh Shishak comes against Jerusalem and takes the treasures of the temple and palace. When Judah's leaders humble themselves, the LORD spares the city from destruction.
events.evidence: Shoshenq I's victory relief at Karnak (Thebes) lists towns he conquered in Israel and Judah, and a fragment of his monument was found at Megiddo.

events.title: Omri builds Samaria
events.summary: After six years in Tirzah, Omri buys the hill of Samaria and builds a new capital. It remains Israel's capital until its fall in 722 BC.

events.title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
events.summary: After three years of drought, Elijah challenges 450 prophets of Baal. The LORD answers by fire and the people fall on their faces, confessing that the LORD is God.

events.title: Elijah at Horeb
events.summary: Fleeing Jezebel, Elijah travels to Horeb, the mountain of God. The LORD speaks to him in a low whisper and tells him seven thousand in Israel have not bowed to Baal.
events.note: The location of Horeb (Sinai) is uncertain; Jebel Musa is the traditional site, but several others have been proposed.

events.title: Battle of Qarqar
events.summary: Ahab joins a coalition of western kings against Shalmaneser III of Assyria at Qarqar, on the Orontes River in Syria. The battle is not recorded in the Bible.
events.evidence: Shalmaneser III's Kurkh Monolith lists "Ahab the Israelite" with 2,000 chariots and 10,000 soldiers. This is one of the two fixed points from which the kings' dates are calculated.

events.title: Ahab dies at Ramoth-gilead
events.summary: Ignoring the prophet Micaiah's warning, Ahab and Jehoshaphat attack Ramoth-gilead. Ahab disguises himself, but an arrow shot at random strikes him and he dies, as the LORD had said.

events.title: Moab rebels
events.summary: Mesha king of Moab stops paying tribute. Joram of Israel, Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom march against him, and Elisha promises water in the desert.
events.evidence: The Mesha Stele (Moabite Stone), now in the Louvre, is Mesha's own account of throwing off Israel's rule.

events.title: Elijah taken up; Elisha succeeds
events.summary: Elijah is taken up to heaven in a whirlwind beyond the Jordan near Jericho. Elisha takes up his cloak and receives a double portion of his spirit.
events.note: 2 Chronicles 21:12 records a letter from Elijah to Jehoram of Judah, so some scholars place this event a few years later.

events.title: Elisha and the Shunammite's son
events.summary: A woman of Shunem gives Elisha a room. The LORD gives her a son, and when the boy dies Elisha raises him to life.

events.title: Chariots of fire at Dothan
events.summary: The king of Aram surrounds Dothan to capture Elisha. Elisha prays, and his servant sees the hills full of horses and chariots of fire.

events.title: Jehu's revolt
events.summary: A prophet sent by Elisha anoints Jehu at Ramoth-gilead. Jehu kills Joram of Israel, Ahaziah of Judah and Jezebel, and destroys Baal worship in Israel.
events.evidence: The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III shows "Jehu son of Omri" paying tribute in 841 BC, the second fixed point for the kings' dates.

events.title: Joash crowned in the temple
events.summary: Athaliah had tried to destroy the royal family, but the infant Joash was hidden in the temple for six years. Jehoiada the priest crowns him, and David's line is preserved.

events.title: Jonah preaches in Nineveh
events.summary: Jonah flees from Joppa toward Tarshish, is swallowed by a great fish, and finally preaches in Nineveh. The city repents and God shows mercy.

events.title: Assyrian eclipse
events.summary: The Assyrian list of yearly officials records a solar eclipse. Astronomers date it to 15 June 763 BC. Not a biblical event, but it fixes Assyrian chronology, and through it the dates of Israel's and Judah's kings.
events.evidence: Assyrian Eponym List: eclipse in the month Simanu, in the year of Bur-Sagale.

events.title: Amos at Bethel; the great earthquake
events.summary: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, prophesies against Israel at Bethel two years before an earthquake still remembered centuries later (Zechariah 14:5).
events.evidence: Excavations at Hazor and other sites show damage from a major earthquake around 760 BC.

events.title: Isaiah's vision
events.summary: In the year King Uzziah dies, Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up, hears the seraphim cry "Holy, holy, holy", and answers, "Here am I. Send me."

events.title: Ahaz turns to Assyria; Damascus falls
events.summary: Rezin of Damascus and Pekah of Israel attack Jerusalem. Isaiah urges Ahaz to trust the LORD and gives the sign of Immanuel, but Ahaz pays Tiglath-pileser instead. Assyria takes Damascus and deports the people of Galilee.

events.title: Fall of Samaria
events.summary: After a three-year siege Assyria captures Samaria and deports Israel to Halah, Gozan and the cities of the Medes. Scripture explains why: Israel had sinned against the LORD and refused to listen to his prophets.
events.evidence: Sargon II's inscriptions claim the capture of Samaria and the deportation of over 27,000 people.

events.title: Sennacherib invades Judah
events.summary: Assyria captures Judah's fortified cities, including Lachish, and threatens Jerusalem. Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD and prays; the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp and Sennacherib returns home.
events.evidence: Sennacherib's prism boasts he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem "like a bird in a cage", but does not claim to have taken the city. Reliefs of the siege of Lachish lined his palace in Nineveh.

events.title: Sennacherib assassinated
events.summary: Sennacherib is killed by his sons while worshipping in Nineveh, as Isaiah had foretold.
events.evidence: The Babylonian Chronicle records Sennacherib's murder by his son in 681 BC.

events.title: The Book of the Law found
events.summary: During temple repairs in Josiah's 18th year the Book of the Law is found. Josiah renews the covenant, removes idolatry and destroys the altar at Bethel, fulfilling the prophecy made 300 years earlier (1 Kings 13:2).

events.title: Fall of Nineveh
events.summary: Babylonians and Medes destroy Nineveh, as Nahum and Zephaniah had foretold.
events.evidence: The Babylonian Chronicle records the capture of Nineveh in 612 BC.

events.title: Josiah killed at Megiddo
events.summary: Pharaoh Neco marches north to help Assyria. Josiah goes out to stop him at Megiddo and is killed. Jeremiah composes a lament for him.

events.title: Battle of Carchemish; Daniel taken
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar defeats Egypt at Carchemish and becomes master of the region. Daniel and his friends are among the first young men taken to Babylon.
events.note: Daniel 1:1 calls this Jehoiakim's third year and Jeremiah 46:2 his fourth: the same year counted in the Babylonian and Judean ways.
events.evidence: The Babylonian Chronicle records the battle of Carchemish in 605 BC.

events.title: Jehoiachin and Ezekiel exiled
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar captures Jerusalem and takes King Jehoiachin, the temple treasures and ten thousand captives to Babylon, including the young priest Ezekiel.
events.evidence: The Babylonian Chronicle dates the capture of "the city of Judah" to 2 Adar, which is 16 March 597 BC.

events.title: Ezekiel's vision by the Chebar
events.summary: In the fifth year of the exile Ezekiel sees the glory of the LORD among the exiles in Babylonia: God has not abandoned his people.

events.title: Jerusalem and the temple destroyed
events.summary: After a long siege, Babylon breaks through Jerusalem's walls. Zedekiah is captured and judged at Riblah; the temple Solomon built is burned and the people are carried into exile.
events.note: Many scholars date this to 587 BC; the one-year difference depends on how Judah's regnal years were counted.

events.title: Jeremiah taken to Egypt
events.summary: After the governor Gedaliah is murdered at Mizpah, the remaining people flee to Egypt against the LORD's word, taking Jeremiah with them to Tahpanhes.

events.title: Jehoiachin released
events.summary: Evil-merodach releases Jehoiachin and gives him a place at the king's table. The books of Kings end on this note of hope for David's line.

events.title: Fall of Babylon
events.summary: On the night of Belshazzar's feast, Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians.
events.evidence: The Nabonidus Chronicle and the Cyrus Cylinder record Cyrus's capture of Babylon in October 539 BC.

events.title: Cyrus's decree: the return
events.summary: In his first year over Babylon, Cyrus allows the Jews to return and rebuild the temple, fulfilling the word of the LORD through Jeremiah and Isaiah.
events.evidence: The Cyrus Cylinder describes his policy of returning exiled peoples to their homelands.

events.title: The first return from exile
events.summary: Nearly 50,000 people return to Judah with the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken, led by Sheshbazzar, Zerubbabel and Jeshua the high priest.

events.title: Altar rebuilt; temple foundation laid
events.summary: The altar is rebuilt and the foundation of the second temple laid. The people shout for joy, while old men who had seen Solomon's temple weep aloud.

events.title: Opposition halts the building
events.summary: When the returned exiles refuse help from the mixed peoples of the land, those people discourage and frighten them. Work on the temple stops until the second year of Darius.

events.title: Haggai and Zechariah: build again
events.summary: The LORD stirs up Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the people through Haggai and Zechariah, and work on the temple resumes.
events.evidence: Babylonian tablets fix the reign of Darius I, so Haggai 1:1 can be dated precisely: 29 August 520 BC.

events.title: Cyrus's decree found at Ecbatana
events.summary: Tattenai, the Persian governor, questions the building. Darius orders a search, and Cyrus's original decree is found in the archives at Ecbatana. Darius confirms it and orders the cost paid from royal revenue.

events.title: The second temple completed
events.summary: The temple is finished on the 3rd of Adar in Darius's 6th year (March 515 BC), about seventy years after Solomon's temple was destroyed. The people dedicate it with joy and keep the Passover.

events.title: Esther becomes queen
events.summary: In the 7th year of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes), Esther is chosen as queen in Susa. On Mordecai's advice she keeps her Jewish identity hidden.

events.title: Haman's plot defeated; Purim
events.summary: Haman plots to destroy every Jew in the empire. Esther risks her life to plead with the king ("who knows whether you have not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?") and the Jews are delivered. The feast of Purim remembers it.
events.evidence: Persian administrative tablets mention an official at Susa named Marduka; some scholars suggest he is Mordecai, though this is not certain.

events.title: Ezra returns to teach the Law
events.summary: Ezra gathers the returning exiles at the Ahava canal, proclaims a fast, and travels to Jerusalem without a royal escort, trusting that "the hand of our God is for good on all who seek him" (Ezra 8:22).
events.note: Dated to the 7th year of Artaxerxes I. Some scholars prefer 398 BC under Artaxerxes II.

events.title: Nehemiah sent to Jerusalem
events.summary: In the citadel of Susa, Nehemiah hears that Jerusalem's walls lie in ruins. He fasts and prays, and in the month of Nisan of Artaxerxes' 20th year the king grants his request to rebuild the city.

events.title: Jerusalem's walls rebuilt in 52 days
events.summary: Despite ridicule and threats from Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem, the people build with one hand and hold a weapon in the other. The wall is finished in 52 days, and even their enemies see that the work was done with the help of God.
events.evidence: Papyri from the Jewish community at Elephantine in Egypt (407 BC) mention "the sons of Sanballat, governor of Samaria" and Johanan the high priest (Nehemiah 12:22), fitting Nehemiah's time under Artaxerxes I.

events.title: Ezra reads the Law; covenant renewed
events.summary: Ezra reads the Book of the Law from early morning until midday while the Levites explain its meaning. The people weep, then celebrate the Feast of Booths, confess their sins, and sign a covenant to keep God's law.

events.title: Nehemiah's second term and reforms
events.summary: After returning to the king in Artaxerxes' 32nd year, Nehemiah comes back to find Tobiah living in a temple storeroom, the Levites unpaid, the Sabbath broken and mixed marriages. He sets each one right.

events.title: Malachi: the Old Testament closes
events.summary: The last Old Testament prophet promises a messenger to prepare the way of the LORD, and Elijah before the great day of the LORD. Four hundred years later the Gospels open with John the Baptist, the messenger Malachi foretold.

leaders.name: Gedaliah
leaders.summary: Appointed governor of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar after Jerusalem fell. Ruled from Mizpah and urged the people to serve Babylon, as Jeremiah counselled. Murdered by Ishmael, a member of the royal family.
leaders.basis: Appointed after the fall of Jerusalem; murdered in the seventh month (Jeremiah 41:1), probably the same year or soon after.

leaders.name: Zerubbabel & Jeshua
leaders.summary: Zerubbabel, grandson of King Jehoiachin, and Jeshua the high priest led the first return and rebuilt the altar and temple. Through Haggai the LORD called Zerubbabel his signet ring, a sign that David's line was not forgotten (Haggai 2:23).
leaders.basis: Led the return under Cyrus; finished the temple in the 6th year of Darius (Ezra 6:15).
leaders.note: Ezra 1:8-11 and 5:14-16 also name Sheshbazzar as the first governor who brought the temple vessels back. Scholars differ on whether he and Zerubbabel were the same person.

leaders.name: Esther & Mordecai
leaders.summary: A Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, Esther became queen of Persia and risked her life to save her people from Haman's plot. God is never named in the book, yet his providence runs through every chapter.
leaders.basis: Made queen in Xerxes' 7th year (Esther 2:16); the deliverance in his 12th year (Esther 3:7).

leaders.name: Ezra
leaders.summary: A priest and scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, who "set his heart to study the Law of the LORD, and to do it and to teach" it in Israel (Ezra 7:10).
leaders.basis: Came to Jerusalem in the 7th year of Artaxerxes (Ezra 7:7-8); still there when the Law was read in 445 BC (Nehemiah 8).
leaders.note: Most evangelical scholars take this as Artaxerxes I (458 BC). Some date Ezra's journey to 398 BC under Artaxerxes II.

leaders.name: Nehemiah
leaders.summary: Cupbearer to Artaxerxes, who prayed, then asked the king for leave to rebuild Jerusalem. As governor he finished the walls in 52 days despite fierce opposition, and led reforms among the people.
leaders.basis: Governor from the 20th to the 32nd year of Artaxerxes (Nehemiah 5:14; 13:6), then returned for a second term.
